whatFailed: The scenario never reached the confirm call: its setup step, POST /v2/bookings with the documented header cal-api-version: 2026-02-25, was silently routed to the 2024-04-15 controller (Cal.diy ships no 2026-02-25 version), whose flat input schema rejected the 2024-08-13 style body with 400 for missing top-level timeZone, language and metadata.

docClaim.quote: Must be set to 2026-02-25. ... <Note>Please make sure to pass in the cal-api-version header value as mentioned in the Headers section. Not passing the correct value will default to an older version of this endpoint.</Note>
docClaim.section: confirm-a-booking/openapi (parameters: cal-api-version, required: true, default '2026-02-25'; operationId BookingsController_2026_02_25_confirmBooking; 200 response GetBookingOutput_2024_08_13)

observed: HTTP 400 in 17 ms with {"status":"error",...,"error":{"code":"BadRequestException","message":"Bad Request Exception","details":{"errors":[{property:"timeZone","isTimeZone"},{property:"language","isString"},{property:"metadata","isObject"}]}}}. The echoed validation target is {"start":"2050-09-08T09:00:00.000Z","eventTypeId":101}, i.e. the nested attendee object was whitelist-stripped before validation, which is the fingerprint of the 2024-04-15 CreateBookingInput. The server log in the same evidence dir shows the route table for this boot: 'BookingsController_2024_04_15 {/v2/bookings} (version: 2024-04-15,2024-06-11,2024-06-14)', 'BookingsController_2024_08_13 {/v2/bookings} (version: 2024-08-13)' and 'Mapped {/v2/bookings/:bookingUid/confirm, POST} (version: 2024-08-13)'. No 2026-02-25 controller is registered.
impact: Nobody is harmed by a Cal.diy bug here; the harm is to the reader of cal.com's public API reference who runs it against Cal.diy: the mandated cal-api-version is not implemented, and instead of an explicit unsupported-version error the request is silently downgraded to a 2024-04-15 endpoint with a different body contract, so the 400 blames the caller's fields rather than the version.

rootCause.explanation: The Nest custom version extractor reads the cal-api-version header and returns it only when it is a member of API_VERSIONS; otherwise it silently returns VERSION_2024_04_15 and that is also the defaultVersion. API_VERSIONS in packages/platform/constants/api.ts:56-68 of the tested tree is exactly [2024-06-14, 2024-06-11, 2024-04-15, 2024-08-13, 2024-09-04], so the documented 2026-02-25 is unknown and the request lands on BookingsController_2024_04_15 (apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-04-15/controllers/bookings.controller.ts:104-106, version [2024-04-15, 2024-06-11, 2024-06-14]). That controller's input, apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-04-15/inputs/create-booking.input.ts:122-146, declares top-level timeZone (@IsTimeZone), language (@IsString) and metadata (@IsObject) as required and has no nested attendee, and the global ValidationPipe runs with whitelist: true, which is precisely the three-error 400 and the stripped target that the evidence shows. There is no 2026_02_25 or 2026_05_01 token anywhere in apps/api/v2/src or packages/platform in the tested tree; the confirm endpoint exists only as BookingsController_2024_08_13.confirmBooking (apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/bookings.controller.ts:470-492), whose own @ApiHeader says 'Must be set to 2024-08-13'. So the product implements the documented confirm contract, just under a version the doc does not mention, while the doc mandates a version the product does not ship.

fixedAfter.note: In cal.diy: no. Only 4 commits landed on origin/main between the tested 038381aeca and 176037d0af (#29940, #29901, #29740, #29819) and none touches packages/platform/constants/api.ts, apps/api/v2/src/bootstrap.ts, apps/api/v2/src/lib/api-versions.ts or the 2024-08-13 bookings controller; API_VERSIONS still tops out at 2024-09-04 and the extractor still downgrades unknown versions to 2024-04-15. The one proposed fix, PR #28561, was closed unmerged on 2026-03-25. In cal.com: not verifiable from source, since the commercial tree is private and the public calcom/cal.com main is byte-identical to calcom/cal.diy main. The public evidence that hosted Cal.com does serve 2026-02-25 is the documentation itself plus the #28561 author's report; there is no public commit to cite.

colleagueFinding.note: None of the five findings in /Users/musheghgevorgyan/repos/cal.diy/docs/guard-findings.md covers this scenario. They concern out-of-office with date overrides (#1), zero-length team slots (#2), a dropped 9:10 override slot (#3), adding an attendee to a seated booking (#4) and unauthenticated slot-hold mutation (#5). This failure is instance #1 of the coordinator's already-established systemic cause, the unsupported cal-api-version header, and my evidence agrees with that framing and adds the per-route runtime proof from the server log.

notes: Two things worth stating for the maintainer and the doc author. (a) Would the scenario also fail on the versions Cal.diy does have? Almost certainly not for step 1: the same run contains a PASSING scenario, read-the-attendees-of-a-booking.api.1, whose first step is the identical create shape ({eventTypeId, start, attendee:{name, email, timeZone}}) with cal-api-version: 2024-08-13 and an expected 201, and it passed. Across the whole scenario corpus the header histogram is 154 uses of 2024-08-13, 61 of 2024-09-04, 139 of 2026-02-25 and 49 of 2026-05-01; only the two 2026 families are affected. Retargeting this scenario to 2024-08-13 is the single-token change that would let it exercise the real behavior. (b) Is there a Cal.diy-side defect in the bound doc claim itself, independent of the version? No evidence of one. The whole documented confirm contract is present in the tested tree: the route exists (POST /v2/bookings/:bookingUid/confirm, @HttpCode(HttpStatus.OK), BOOKING_WRITE permission, ApiAuthGuard + BookingUidGuard, no request body), it returns GetBookingOutput_2024_08_13, and the output DTO in packages/platform/types/bookings/2024-08-13/outputs/booking.output.ts carries every field the scenario asserts, including the required description, hosts[].displayEmail (line 35), attendees[].displayEmail (line 106) and icsUid (line 287). Cal.diy's own e2e suite, apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/e2e/confirm-bookings.e2e-spec.ts:118-175, drives exactly this endpoint at 2024-08-13 and asserts 200, status success and data.status 'accepted' with the DB row moving to ACCEPTED. So the confirm claim is untested by this run rather than falsified, and a re-run at 2024-08-13 is what would settle whether the response shape assertions (notably data.description, data.bookingFieldsResponses and the attendees[0].language enum) hold at runtime. Finally, the docs and the product disagree with each other in a way a doc author can fix cheaply: the doc's parameter says 'Must be set to 2026-02-25' while the shipped controller's own ApiHeader says 'Must be set to 2024-08-13', and the doc's own 200 schema is still named GetBookingOutput_2024_08_13, so even the commercial reference is only partially re-versioned.
